faqs.a: Admission runs through the National Defense University (MSÜ) under the Ministry of National Defense, which has overseen the Army, Naval and Air Force academies since 2016. Candidates sit the ÖSYM-run MSÜ selection exam and must also take the YKS university entrance exams (TYT and AYT) and reach the required ranking.
faqs.q: How do you apply to the Turkish Military Academy?

faqs.a: Applicants must be Turkish citizens, generally under 21 on 1 January of the entry year, high school graduates or final-year students expecting to graduate, unmarried and never previously married. They must pass a physical fitness test, strict medical standards and a security background check, with a strong record in science and mathematics.
faqs.q: What are the eligibility requirements for MSÜ?

faqs.a: The education lasts five years including a preparatory year, combining academic study with military training. Graduates are commissioned as officers in the Turkish Land Forces and other branches with a bachelor's degree, and must then serve 15 years. The academy enrols roughly 4,000 cadets.
faqs.q: How long is the programme and what happens after graduation?

faqs.a: Candidates who meet the exam score thresholds are invited to the second selection stage, announced on the Ministry of National Defense recruitment portal. This stage includes physical fitness tests, medical examinations and interviews before final placement. Final admission is competitive and based on combined rankings.

headline: Turkish Military Academy Requirements 2026: MSÜ Exam, Eligibility and Training
metaDescription: Turkish Military Academy admissions 2026: MSÜ exam via ÖSYM, YKS TYT and AYT requirement, age and fitness standards, second selection stage, 5-year officer programme.

sections.content:
Since the 2016 restructuring, the Turkish Military Academy, Naval Academy and Air Force Academy all sit under the National Defense University (MSÜ – Milli Savunma Üniversitesi), part of the Ministry of National Defense. It is the sole route to a commission as an officer in the Turkish Armed Forces.

Entry begins with the MSÜ selection exam run by ÖSYM, the national student selection body. Applications are submitted online and the exam is typically held in February, with results published in March. In recent cycles more than 600,000 candidates sat the exam, so competition is intense and preparation should start well in advance.
sections.title: The MSÜ system and the selection exam

sections.content:
Candidates must also sit the YKS university entrance exams – the Basic Proficiency Test (TYT) and the Field Proficiency Test (AYT) – and achieve the required success ranking, since admissions are aligned with the national higher-education timeline.

Eligibility rules are strict: Turkish citizenship, generally under 21 on 1 January of the entry year, high school graduate or final-year student, unmarried and never previously married. Candidates must pass a physical fitness test, rigorous medical standards and a security background check, with strong science and mathematics results expected.
sections.title: Eligibility: age, education and fitness standards

sections.content:
Those who clear the score thresholds are called to the second selection stage, announced on the defence ministry's recruitment portal. This stage combines physical fitness tests, detailed medical examinations and interviews before final placement decisions are made.

Successful candidates enter a five-year programme including a preparatory year, blending academic study with military training. On graduation they receive a bachelor's degree and a commission as an officer, followed by a compulsory 15-year service commitment. Around 4,000 cadets are enrolled at the academy.
sections.title: Second selection stage and the five-year programme

sections.content:
The MSÜ route suits students who want a fully funded, structured path to an officer's career rather than civilian university. Because the exam cycle follows the academic year, candidates should track ÖSYM announcements from early in the year and prepare for both the MSÜ exam and the YKS in parallel.

Note that exact 2026 exam dates had not been published in the sources reviewed; they follow the established pattern of early-year applications and a February exam. Always confirm dates on the official ÖSYM portal before planning travel or leave.
